title: interpolating a foreign value calls its `Symbol.toPrimitive`/`toString`, so a template literal is a foreign call
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." The coercion protocol is the third of the three the position predicate recognises. Interpolation looks like formatting and is a method call on a foreign object; `${x}` runs `x[Symbol.toPrimitive]()` or `x.toString()`, both of which the foreign module owns. The complementary acceptance is 09-foreign-calls/a-trusted-bindings-string-may-still-be-interpolated-and-iterated, which keeps the rule from widening to a trusted binding's primitive.
